$comment: Shared vectors for how a published check is evaluated. The Hajer platform's check interpreter and the SDK's CI evaluator (hajer.pytest_plugin) must give every vector the same answer.

splitting.SENTENCES: runs ended by one or more of . ! ? (regex [^.!?]*[.!?]+|[^.!?]+$ over the stripped text), plus a trailing run with no terminator; every period is a boundary, so 'Use a tool, e.g. a hammer' is three sentences ('Use a tool, e.' 'g.' ' a hammer')
splitting.PARAGRAPHS: blocks of the stripped text separated by a newline, optional whitespace, and a newline (regex \n\s*\n); blank blocks are not counted
splitting.CHARACTERS_AND_ITEMS: length with no unit: a string's characters, a list's items, an object's keys

notApplicable: A check whose applicability does not hold leaves the reply out of its requirement's scope: the requirement holds, so CI reads it PASS (never FAIL).

sentences: e.g. is two boundaries (3 sentences)

absence: An absent field fails every operation but not_contains: an absent field holds no prohibited text, so a prohibition is kept by leaving the field out. null is a present value (exists holds) and is not text.
outsideTheList: A vector marked outsideTheList uses an operation generation never publishes: the backend answers it, the CI evaluator does not (UNABLE_TO_VERIFY), which is why the generator refuses to publish it.

toolCallSubjects.name: openai JSON content beside a tool call keeps both
a tool loop ending in a text answer keeps the tool call
a tool loop ending in a JSON answer keeps both
a text-only reply has no tool calls
a tool called twice in one reply is ambiguous
a tool called in two replies of a loop is ambiguous
arguments that are not an object
a tool reply cut at max_tokens

toolCallSubject: A reply's tool calls (the model's structured form) join its subject as {"tool_calls": {<tool name>: {"arguments": <decoded arguments object>}}}, gathered from every reply of the attempt: the reply that carries the named call, not the attempt's last reply, so a tool loop ending in a text answer keeps the call. A name called more than once in the attempt, arguments that are not an object, and a reply cut at its token limit give that name no entry. The text subject (the last reply's one text block decoded as a JSON object) stays beside it. A structured-output rule (subject stage TOOL_ARGUMENTS) is checked at output.tool_calls.<name>.arguments.<field>; in CI such a check reads the case's recorded replies, every other check the application's return value.
missingToolCall: A check path under output.tool_calls.<name> when the subject holds no call to <name> is unknown (UNSCORED_MISSING_OBSERVATION, CI UNABLE_TO_VERIFY), never absent: the reply may simply not have made the call. A field absent inside a call that is present follows the absence rule.
documentOperations: schema_valid, grounded, excludes and fields_compare carry their parameters in valueJson (the platform's document and grounding predicates; the SDK's hajer/pytest_plugin/_documents.py and _grounding.py). grounded's claims are named rules: URL and EMAIL (whole tokens), DATE (month and day, any listed format), NUMBER (whole tokens, commas and trailing zeros dropped, number words and DERIVED_ARITHMETIC ground them); names are NAMES_LEFT_TO_JUDGE and line-start list markers are LIST_MARKER, never claims. excludes matches whole words, case-folded on both sides; a term in a script written without spaces (CJK, Thai, kana …) matches anywhere.

metamorphicRelations: INV passes when the base check gives the edited input's reply the verdict it gave the original (with keep: when the named output field is unchanged); DIR passes when the base check holds on the edited reply. Relations and judge checks run live only; a replay lists them under liveOnly (METAMORPHIC_NEEDS_LIVE, JUDGE_NEEDS_LIVE), never a pass.
